findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — P1 confidence 100: `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` commits the database before the external calendar transition at line 165, so any provider rejection leaves durable attendees absent from the calendar and a retry cannot repair the drift because those addresses are filtered as already present.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — P1 confidence 100 coupling advisory: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` binds calendar synchronization to the invoking attendee/admin even though the event and destination calendar belong to `booking.user`, so permitted non-organizer callers update with unrelated provider credentials; the strongest rebuttal is that EventManager may select by destination calendar, but it cannot use an organizer credential that was never loaded.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124 — P1 confidence 100 wrong-shape advisory: `const evt: CalendarEvent = {` manually rebuilds only a subset of the booking event and omits `team`, while `sendAddGuestsEmails` branches on `calendarEvent.team?.members`, so team bookings silently skip every team-member notification; the strongest rebuttal is that the primary organizer still receives mail, but that does not satisfy the explicitly implemented team-recipient branch.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — P1 confidence 100: `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` accepts duplicate and unbounded addresses, and the handler's `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)` never deduplicates the request itself, so direct API callers can create duplicate attendee rows and fan out an unbounded calendar update plus email burst.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — P2 confidence 100: `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...));` requires both roles and therefore rejects a team administrator who is not the owner, contradicting the variable and the existing role boundary implied by “admin or owner.”

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525 — P2 confidence 75 simplification advisory: `export const sendAddGuestsEmails = async (calEvent: CalendarEvent, newGuests: string[]) => {` creates a parallel notification orchestrator instead of extending the established event-update email policy path, and deleting this bespoke branch in favor of the common policy-aware dispatcher would prevent configuration and recipient semantics from drifting; the strongest rebuttal is that guest-specific templates need a distinct message, but template selection does not require duplicating dispatch policy.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525 — P1 confidence 100: `export const sendAddGuestsEmails = async (calEvent: CalendarEvent, newGuests: string[]) => {` accepts no event-type metadata and unconditionally queues both host and attendee mail, so the sibling user-config gates `disableStandardEmails.all.host` and `disableStandardEmails.all.attendee` at lines 82–86 are not propagated and opted-out users are notified.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — P1 confidence 100: `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` commits the new attendee rows before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`, so any calendar-update failure leaves the database and provider split-brained and a retry cannot repair it because lines 74–81 filter those now-persisted addresses and throw `BAD_REQUEST` when none remain.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — P2 confidence 75: `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(` only excludes addresses already present in the pre-write booking and does not deduplicate the submitted array (while the server schema is merely `guests: z.array(z.string().email())`), so direct/replayed requests containing the same address twice create duplicate attendee records and propagate duplicate attendee data to the calendar provider.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — P1 confidence 100: `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` commits the guests before the fallible `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` at line 165, so a calendar-provider failure returns an error after persistence and every retry deterministically fails at `uniqueGuests.length === 0`, leaving the booking database and external calendar permanently divergent.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — P1 confidence 100: `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` persists guests before the fallible `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` at line 165, so a provider failure returns an error after committing and the retry hits `uniqueGuests.length === 0`, permanently leaving the calendar stale even if database writes are normally reliable because the exact trigger is any later calendar rejection.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — P1 confidence 100: `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` converts total or partial notification failure into `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the UI reports success while recipients silently receive no update; calendar invitations do not rebut this because this separate email fan-out explicitly supplies both new-guest confirmations and existing-attendee notices.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — P1 confidence 100: `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` has no length cap and flows into one database row, one translation load, and one outbound email per resulting attendee, so a single request with a large guest list amplifies into unbounded request-path work and can exhaust the server or exceed its deadline even if ordinary UI submissions stay small because the endpoint itself accepts arbitrarily large arrays.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — P2 confidence 100: `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(` only filters against pre-existing attendees and never deduplicates the submitted array, so a client sending the same valid address twice creates duplicate attendee rows and duplicate calendar/email recipients even though the current dialog rejects duplicates because any alternate or racing client can call the server schema directly.

packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:27 — P2 confidence 100: `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)],` grows an SMTP header with every attendee, so once a booking accumulates enough guests the organizer notification exceeds provider header/address limits and is silently dropped by the handler; providers accepting today's small lists does not survive the exact trigger of a sufficiently large booking because neither this header nor guest additions are capped.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:40 — P2 confidence 75: `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate();` is an unawaited promise inside an async success callback, so a cache invalidation/refetch rejection becomes unhandled after the dialog has already shown success and closed, leaving stale booking state invisible to the user.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — P3 confidence 100: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` is always a nonempty string even when the structured code/message is absent, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never render its fallback and transport/unknown failures surface as an `undefined:` error instead of actionable feedback.

apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx:194 — P1 confidence 75: `id: "add_members"` exposes only an add-guests action, so the stated requirement to "Add guest management functionality" is under-scoped because users receive no operation to remove or otherwise manage guests already attached to an existing booking.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:54 — P1 confidence 100: `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` authorizes any attendee to add arbitrary email addresses and trigger organizer-branded calendar invitations containing the booking details and video-call credentials, so a malicious attendee can impersonate the organizer to spam or disclose the private meeting to third parties.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows line 27 in organizer-add-guests-email.ts creates a replyTo header that includes the organizer email plus ALL attendee emails: `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`. This array grows with every attendee added to the booking. SMTP headers have size limits (typically 998 characters per line per RFC 5321, and providers often have address count limits). The finding correctly identifies that as guests accumulate, this header could exceed provider limits. However, the confidence of 100% is overstated since the exact threshold depends on provider limits and typical booking sizes. The issue is real but the severity depends on actual usage patterns. This is a legitimate edge-case bug where the code doesn't cap the number of addresses in the replyTo header.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:40 — P2 confidence 75: `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate();` is an unawaited promise inside an async success callback, so a cache invalidation/refetch rejection becomes unhandled after the dialog has already shown success and closed, leaving stale booking state invisible to the user.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that not awaiting `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` causes unhandled promise rejections. However, in React Query/tRPC patterns, `invalidate()` is commonly called without await in success callbacks - it triggers a background refetch and any errors would be handled by React Query's error handling mechanisms, not cause unhandled rejections. The dialog closing and showing success is the correct behavior - the cache invalidation happens asynchronously. This is a standard pattern in tRPC/React Query codebases and not a bug. The finding mischaracterizes normal async cache invalidation as problematic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — P3 confidence 100: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` is always a nonempty string even when the structured code/message is absent, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never render its fallback and transport/unknown failures surface as an `undefined:` error instead of actionable feedback.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the template literal `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` will always produce a non-empty string (at minimum ': ' or 'undefined: something') even when err.data?.code is undefined. This means the fallback `|| t('unable_to_add_guests')` will never be reached, and users could see confusing error messages like 'undefined: error_key' instead of the intended fallback. This is a real bug in the error handling logic shown in the diff at lines 41-42 of AddGuestsDialog.tsx.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx:194 — P1 confidence 75: `id: "add_members"` exposes only an add-guests action, so the stated requirement to "Add guest management functionality" is under-scoped because users receive no operation to remove or otherwise manage guests already attached to an existing booking.

adjudication.rationale: The finding criticizes the PR for not implementing guest removal functionality, but this is a scope/feature request rather than a defect in the implemented code. The PR clearly implements 'add guests' functionality as shown in the diff - it adds AddGuestsDialog, addGuests handler, and related email templates. The finding assumes a requirement to implement full 'guest management' but the diff shows the feature is specifically scoped to adding guests. There's no evidence in the diff of a stated requirement for removal functionality, and the code correctly implements what it sets out to do.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:54 — P1 confidence 100: `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` authorizes any attendee to add arbitrary email addresses and trigger organizer-branded calendar invitations containing the booking details and video-call credentials, so a malicious attendee can impersonate the organizer to spam or disclose the private meeting to third parties.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the authorization check at line 54 allows any attendee (isAttendee) to add guests. The isAttendee check only verifies if the user's email matches any attendee email. This means any existing attendee can add arbitrary email addresses as guests, which triggers sendAddGuestsEmails() that sends organizer-branded calendar invitations with booking details and potentially video call credentials (videoCallReference is included in evt). This is a legitimate security concern - attendees should typically not have permission to add other guests without organizer approval, as it could be used for spam or unauthorized disclosure of meeting details.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — P1 confidence 100: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no recipient-count limit, so one authenticated request can force arbitrarily large attendee inserts, calendar-provider updates, and outbound-email fan-out, exhausting application/provider resources and creating a bulk-spam primitive.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ZAddGuestsInputSchema with `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` having no length limit. The handler in addGuests.handler.ts processes all guests by creating database records, updating calendar attendees via EventManager, and sending emails to all guests via sendAddGuestsEmails. An authenticated user could submit thousands of email addresses in a single request, causing resource exhaustion through bulk database inserts, calendar API calls, and email sending. This is a real security/DoS vulnerability.
